subject.title: feat(queue): persist followup queues across gateway restarts

question: Should OpenClaw make follow-up queues durable across abrupt gateway restarts with the explicitly documented at-least-once replay contract, or defer this behavior until channel-level idempotency is designed?
rationale: The implementation creates a persistent core delivery contract and deliberately accepts a crash-window replay tradeoff; code review alone cannot choose that product reliability boundary.

options.title: Accept bounded at-least-once recovery
options.body: Merge after a fresh rebase and proof refresh, documenting that a crash between external send and SQLite acknowledgement may replay one queued follow-up.

options.title: Require idempotent delivery first
options.body: Pause this PR until a channel-level idempotency or acknowledgement design can remove the accepted replay window.

options.title: Narrow to migration groundwork
options.body: Keep the migration and generic storage seam only if maintainers want to defer gateway wake and delivery behavior to a later recovery design.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded at-least-once recovery
recommendation.body: Merge after a fresh rebase and proof refresh, documenting that a crash between external send and SQLite acknowledgement may replay one queued follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied timeline connects this person to the restart-recovery discussion and adjacent gateway work.
